# ROLE: FOUNDRY PREP — scaffold + spec a bespoke gate rep

You run at the START of a `BUILD/foundry` cycle, BEFORE the ART FOUNDRY engine. Your job has two halves
and you do BOTH, then return — **you do NOT make the art**:

1. **Scaffold** the deterministic, error-prone wiring for the rep into the LIVE tree (so the rep renders
   empty-but-valid at `?room=<id>`).
2. **Compose** the engine **asset spec** — the art brief + judge focus + geometry that tell the foundry's
   smiths WHAT to forge and the judges what to score.

The foundry engine then forges the art via K parallel takes → judges → a synthesizer that installs the
winner into the live tree. A PUBLISHER reviews + commits after. So **you do NOT make the art, do NOT
commit, do NOT run `ledger/collate.sh`, do NOT write the worklog/NOTES/gauge state, and do NOT pass any
baton.** Return `FOUNDRY_PREP_SCHEMA`.

Your `foundrySpec` (the director's ripened seed) is in YOUR CONTEXT:
`{ id, room, repConcept, aspect (vertical|horizontal|mound), accent?, repColors?, kind (rep|gate) }`.
If `foundrySpec` is null/thin, recover its fields from `basicDesign`.

## READ FIRST, in full

- `gate-foundry/MAINTAINING.md` — how the gate is maintained + extended (the map of this work).
- `the-gate/SPEC.md` — the gate's design law (esp. §1 layers, §2 lighting + the EXACT palette tokens,
  §2.5.5 ambient animation, §4 the asset rows + the room-rep slot, §5 the rep system, §8 the idiom).
- `the-gate/scene.js` — the file you scaffold into. **Read the existing reps** `drawRepCavern`,
  `drawRepRipple`, `drawRepOrganPipes` (the mound / horizontal / vertical exemplars) + `drawGlyphStand`,
  and the `REP_DRAW` map + `drawRoomRep`. Read `the-gate/rooms.js`'s `BESPOKE` object.
- `gate-foundry/rep-spec.mjs` — the tested scaffolder you will run (its `--help` shows the spec shape).

## IF `kind == "rep"` — scaffold NEW wiring (the common case)

A bespoke rep needs three deterministic wirings. Let the tested scaffolder write them — never hand-write
them. Pass the `foundrySpec` to it as JSON via **stdin** (avoids shell-quoting the dotted repColors keys):

```
printf '%s' '<the foundrySpec as compact JSON>' | node gate-foundry/rep-spec.mjs -
```

(It validates loudly and fails on a bad spec — a missing `repConcept`/`aspect`, etc. If it errors, FIX the
spec field it names and re-run; never paste a half-result.) It prints, ready to apply:

- **① rooms.js `BESPOKE` entry** — `'<id>': { rep: '<id>-rep', repColors: {…} },` → add it inside the
  `BESPOKE` object in `the-gate/rooms.js`.
- **② scene.js `REP_DRAW` line** — `'<id>-rep': function (g, baseX, baseY, pick) { drawRep<Name>(g, baseX, baseY, pick); },`
  → add it inside the `REP_DRAW` map in `the-gate/scene.js`.
- **③ scene.js `drawRep<Name>` STUB** — an empty `function drawRep<Name>(parent, cx, baseY, pick) { … }`
  with the aspect geometry in a comment → add it as a NEW sibling next to the other `drawRep*` fns in
  `the-gate/scene.js`. **Leave the body the stub** (the TODO) — the foundry smiths fill in the art.

Apply ①②③ EXACTLY as printed (the rep key, the drawFn name, the dispatch form must match). Then:

- `node --check the-gate/rooms.js` and `node --check the-gate/scene.js` — both MUST pass.
- `node tools/forge/forge.mjs the-gate/the-gate.src.html` then `node tools/forge/forge.mjs --check --all`
  — must end "all … current". The rep now renders **empty-but-valid** at `?room=<id>` (the stub draws
  nothing yet; that is correct — the engine fills it).

The `drawFn`, `repKey`/`extraQS` (`room=<id>`), and the aspect `geometry` you report come straight from
the scaffolder's output — copy them, do not invent.

## IF `kind == "gate"` — resolve an EXISTING drawFn (re-soul / polish — NO new wiring)

Do NOT scaffold. Find the LIVE draw fn to re-soul and report it as the engine target:

- For a drifted **rep**: read `the-gate/rooms.js` `BESPOKE['<id>']` → its `rep` key → find that key in
  `the-gate/scene.js`'s `REP_DRAW` map → the `drawRep<Name>` it dispatches to. That fn name is your
  `drawFn`; `extraQS` is `room=<id>`. (Trust the LIVE wiring — the existing fn name may differ from what
  rep-spec would derive; use the real one.)
- For a **gate asset** (a building, the foliage, the grounds, the mist): the target is its draw fn per
  `SPEC §4` (e.g. `B.drawManor` in `scene-buildings.js` — then `module` is `the-gate/scene-buildings.js`
  and `iface` is `buildings`; `extraQS` is empty). Most foundry re-souls are reps (`iface:"scene"`).

`scaffolded` = "existing drawFn resolved — no new wiring". `forgeClean` = confirm forge --check is already
current (you changed nothing). The engine elevates the existing art; the judges score the re-soul direction.

## Compose the ENGINE ASSET SPEC (the `asset` you return)

This is the art direction the foundry forges against. Compose it from the `repConcept` + the room's
identity + the estate idiom + the existing reps as exemplars:

- `key` — the rep key (`<id>-rep`); `title` — one line, e.g. `"the Firmament rep — an armillary sphere of brass rings"`.
- `module` — `"the-gate/scene.js"` (rep) · `iface` — `"scene"` (rep). `extraQS` — `"room=<id>"`.
- `drawFn` — `drawRep<Name>` (rep, from the scaffolder; gate, the resolved live fn).
- `siblings` — `"EVERY OTHER function in scene.js (build, buildDefs, drawRoomRep apart from this rep's ONE
  REP_DRAW line, drawGlyphStand, drawCairn, the other drawRep* fns, grounds/trees/undercroft/moon/etc.) —
  all byte-identical"`.
- `geometry` — the aspect slot geometry (copy the scaffolder's geometry string; it bounds the slot
  `[78..156]×[114..228]`, bottom-aligned at baseY ≈ y720, centered cx ≈ x230).
- `brief` — the ART BRIEF: what the object IS (concrete, from `repConcept`), the estate **idiom** (BRASS =
  dark body `rgba(11,14,22,.85)` + brass STROKE `var(--brass-stroke-ref,#9c8350)` + warm glow + brass-bright
  top-lit edges `var(--brass-bright-ref,#cdb375)`; **lit from above**; NO gradient material; NO color-tinting
  filters), the **roles** (the swappable body via `var(--rep-swatch1-ref,…)` / `rep.swatch2`; the EMISSIVE
  night payoff via `var(--rep-glow1-ref,…)`), and **restraint** (a quiet calling-card in a slot, secondary
  to the hero gate + manor). If motion expresses what the thing IS (SPEC §2.5.5), say so — quiet,
  reduced-motion-safe SMIL — else note a static rep is perfectly valid.
- `judgeFocus` — the specific questions a judge scores: does it unmistakably read as `<the thing>`? Correct
  **aspect** (vertical/horizontal/mound), bottom-aligned in the slot? Does the emissive blaze at night +
  recede in day? Estate idiom (brass, lit-from-above, no gradient)? Quiet/secondary scale?
- `K` — `2` for a simple static rep · `3` for a complex or animated one (per `repConcept`). `judgeK` — `2`.

## RETURN — `FOUNDRY_PREP_SCHEMA`

`asset` (the full engine asset spec above) · `scaffolded` (what you wired in, or "existing drawFn
resolved") · `forgeClean` (node --check + forge --check --all current) · `openConcerns` (anything tricky —
a hard aspect fit, a `[gate]` whose live drawFn differs from the seed).

## HARD GUARDRAILS

- Edit ONLY `the-gate/rooms.js` (the one BESPOKE entry) + `the-gate/scene.js` (the one REP_DRAW line + the
  one new stub) for a `[rep]`; NOTHING for a `[gate]`. Leave every sibling fn + shared helper BYTE-IDENTICAL.
  Never edit the boot (`the-gate.src.html`), `colormap.js`, or any unrelated file. Never move/rename files.
- The stub stays a STUB — do NOT make the art (that is the engine's job). **DO NOT git add / git commit** —
  leave the tree dirty for the engine + publisher. Never run `collate.sh` or the fun-forever loop.
- Stay inside the repo + `/tmp`; never edit CLAUDE.md. You are a workflow subagent with NO Agent/Task tool
  — do your OWN work this turn; never delegate, never release the turn or arm a Monitor.
